chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Najran, from Asim ibn Humayd, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him)

Regarding a mukatab (slave manumitted for a fixed payment) under whom was a free woman, and she bequeathed to him upon her death with a bequest. The inheritors said, 'We do not validate her bequest to him, for he is a mukatab who has not been fully freed, and he does not inherit.' So he (peace be upon him) judged that he inherits by the accounting of what was freed from him, and it is valid for him from the bequest by the accounting of what was freed from him.
And he (peace be upon him) judged regarding a mukatab who was bequeathed a bequest, and he had paid half of what was upon him, so he validated half of the bequest.
And he (peace be upon him) judged regarding a mukatab who paid a quarter of what was upon him, and he was bequeathed a bequest, so he validated a quarter of the bequest.

And he (peace be upon him) said regarding a free man who bequeathed to a mukatabah (slave woman), and she had paid a sixth of what was upon her, so he validated for her by the accounting of what was freed from her.

key_terms.مُكَاتَب: A slave who has entered into a contract with their master to pay a specific sum for their manumission
key_terms.مُكَاتَبَةٍ: A female slave under manumission contract

ai.seo_question: How is a bequest validated for a slave who is in the process of paying for their freedom?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the proportional validity of bequests for a mukatab, resolving the dispute among heirs who argued that an unfreed slave cannot inherit. The Imam (peace be upon him) establishes that the bequest is valid to the extent of the slave's emancipation, reflecting the Shia principle that legal capacity accrues gradually with the fulfillment of contractual obligations. This ruling underscores the practical application of justice in personal status law, ensuring that the mukatab's partial freedom is legally recognized in financial transactions.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Najran, from Aasim Bin Hameed, from Muhammad Bin Qays,

(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> regarding a contracted one under who was a free woman. So she bequeathed to him, during her death, with a bequest. So the inheritors said, ‘We do not allow her bequest to him. He is a contracted one and has not been liberated, and he does not inherit. So he<sup>asws</sup> judged that he would inherit by the accounting of what he is liberated from it, and it would be allowed for him from the bequest with the accounting of what he had been freed from it (the contract)’.
And he<sup>asws</sup> judged regard a contracted to who had been bequeathed with a bequest, and he had fulfilled half of what was upon him. So half the bequest would be allowed.
And he<sup>asws</sup> judged regarding a contracted one who had fulfilled a quarter of what was upon him, so he was bequeathed to with a bequest, so he was allowed a quarter of the bequest.

And he<sup>asws</sup> said regarding a free man who had bequeathed to a contracted woman, and he had fulfilled a sixth of what was upon him, so he allowed for her by the accounting of what she was free from it (the contract)’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu Najran from ‘Asem ibn Humayd from Muhammad ibn Qays who has narrated the following:

“This is about the case of a contracted slave who is married to a free woman who in her will assigns something for him and the heirs disagree with her will, saying that he is not free but is only contracted and he cannot inherit. Abu Ja’far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, issued a judgment that he inherits proportionate to the degree of his freedom according to the contract.

He (the Imam), ‘Alayhi al-Salam, judged in the case of a contracted slave for whom a will was made and the slave had paid one-half according to the contract. The judgment granted him one-half of the will.
He (the Imam), ‘Alayhi al-Salam, judged one-fourth of the amount of will in favor of the slave who had paid one-fourth of the amount required according to the contract.

About the case of a free man who had made a will for a contracted slave-girl who had paid one-sixth of what was required according to the contract, He (the Imam), ‘Alayhi al- Salam, judged in her favor proportionate to what was made free from her.
